description:
Scryber.Core is the open-source PDF rendering engine behind Paperwork.Core. It turns HTML templates with CSS styles and SVG drawing, bound to your data, into PDF documents - with flowing pages, data binding, and referenced images, stylesheets and fonts - on .NET and in Blazor WASM.

Paperwork.Core is its successor and the recommended package for new projects. It adds a fluent builder, dependency injection and code configuration on top of this same engine, and your templates carry straight across.

Scryber.Core still works as it always has, and will continue to be maintained and supported. It is released under the LGPL licence, so you can use it in commercial applications.
releaseNotes:
9.11.0
Fixed: a complete html document bound into an iframe (with data-content or src) was not unwrapped when there was whitespace around it, such as a new line after the doctype. It was laid out as a document within the page, and generation failed with 'No Current group on the stack to unregister' (GitHub issue #179).
Changed: a complete html document bound with data-content into any other element, such as a div, now gives a clear error that names the element and says to use an iframe. In strict conformance it is an exception; in lax it is an error in the trace log and the content is left out. Before, it failed later with 'No Current group on the stack to unregister'.
Breaking change: an svg image (img src='image.svg') with a percentage width or height on its svg root (e.g. width='100%' viewBox='0 0 24 24') is sized as a browser - a percentage is not a size of its own, so the image fills the width available with the ratio of the viewBox (or uses the other, absolute, dimension with that ratio). It was sized as the percentage of the viewBox. Give the img a width or height to size it.
Fixed: a style attribute on an svg gradient stop (e.g. style='stop-color: red') stopped the whole document from parsing. The stroke-dashoffset and opacity attributes were only read from css, and a rect did not read its stroke-opacity or stroke-linejoin attributes - they are now read on svg shapes, as their css properties are (opacity is the fill opacity, as the css property).
Fixed: mode() only took numbers - text (e.g. mode(model.choices) of 'A', 'B', 'A') raised an error. Text is now compared as text, and numbers (or text that is a number) as numbers.
Fixed: an empty string with && || ! or the if() function raised an error (e.g. '' && true). These now use the same truth as the ? : operator - null, false, 0, '' and 'false' are false, and other values are true.
Fixed: string() of a collection gave the name of its type (System.Object[]). It is now its items in square brackets, e.g. [1, 2, 3].
Fixed: integer() and long() of text with a fraction (e.g. integer('10.6'), as json values often are) raised an error. The text is read as a number (invariant), then rounded as a number is - 11.
Fixed: a gradient (linear or radial) on a transformed shape or element - an svg shape with a transform, or a block with a css transform such as rotate - stayed where the shape was before it was transformed, so it was not rotated or moved with the shape, and clipped it (a moved svg shape could disappear). The gradient now has the transformation of its shape.
New: embedded TrueType fonts can be subset - only the outlines of the glyphs used are embedded, so a short document with a large font is much smaller (Segoe UI regular and bold: about 2MB to under 100KB). It is off by default: set Scryber:Fonts:SubsetEmbeddedFonts to true in the configuration, or document.RenderOptions.SubsetEmbeddedFonts, or for one HTML template add <meta name="font-subset" content="true" /> to the head. The glyph numbers and the text are unchanged, so text can still be selected and searched. A font with CFF outlines, or whose licence does not allow subsetting (OS/2 fsType 0x0100), is embedded in full with a warning in the trace log (GitHub issue #202). Requires Scryber.Core.OpenType 9.11.0.
Breaking change: lists are indented as css - the indent is the padding-left of the ul or ol (30pt, 40px, by default), and the marker sits in that padding, just before the text (0.3 of the font size). Items were indented 40pt in addition to any padding of the list, so a list moves 10pt to the left, padding-left: 0 hangs the markers outside the list, and padding-left: 15pt is a 15pt indent (it was 55pt). -pdf-li-inset is now how far the marker box reaches back from the text, rather than an extra indent - use padding-left to make room for wide markers. A dd is indented 30pt (40px), not 40pt.
New: list markers are drawn as a browser draws them - list-style-type disc, circle and square are a filled circle, a hollow circle and a filled square, in the colour of the text, sized and placed from the font (0.31em, 0.15em above the baseline). A bulleted list is a disc, a list nested in another list is a circle, and deeper lists are squares, unless a list-style-type is set. The bullet was a small character, the same at every depth, and circle and square were drawn as it.
Changed: an absolute, fixed, floating or inline-block element without a width is the width of its content (as css shrink-to-fit) when that content is blocks (e.g. a div or p) - it filled the space to the right of the page. The blocks inside fill the width of the widest. Content that is wider than the space available (its text wraps) fills the space, limited by any max-width - including text on its own, which was the width of its widest line. A wrapped inline-block therefore fills the line, and moves to a line of its own. A table inside keeps the width of its columns, as before.
Fixed: a space that did not fit at the end of a line (e.g. after an inline-block that fills the line) was carried to the start of the next line, indenting its text. It is dropped, as a browser does.
New: paint-order on svg shapes (as an attribute or css) - paint-order: stroke draws the stroke before the fill, so the fill covers the inner half of the stroke. It was only used by html blocks.
Fixed: a pattern fill on a transformed svg shape (e.g. transform='rotate(20)') stayed where the shape was before it was transformed. The pattern tiles now move, turn and scale with the shape, as gradients.
Fixed: an svg image larger than the space available was drawn at 300 x 150, as its size was read before the svg was laid out. It is now reduced to fit, keeping its ratio, as other images.
Fixed: an svg image with only a viewBox, reduced to fit the height left on a page, kept the full width and lost its ratio. It now keeps the ratio of the viewBox.

9.10.0
New: the conditional (ternary) operator in expressions - condition ? whenTrue : whenFalse, e.g. {{model.count == 1 ? 'item' : 'items'}}. It has the lowest precedence, a chain reads from the right (a ? b : c ? d : e), and only the chosen value is evaluated. A condition is false when it is null, false, zero, an empty string or the text 'false'. The javascript forms === and !== are also read as == and !=.
Fixed: a style block (or the document styles) with more than 30 rules ignored @page rules - including :first, named pages and @page inside @media - so the page size and margins were not set (issue #200, found by Matthias Voigt). With more than 30 rules the later of two rules with the same specificity also did not always win (e.g. .a and .b on class='b a'), and a document with more than 30 style or link elements failed with an error. A large block now gives the same result as a small one.
Fixed: Newtonsoft (JObject) and System.Text.Json models now bind the same way in expressions - all JSON values are read in one place. An item from a Newtonsoft array (e.g. model.tags[1]) is now its value (a string, number or bool), not a JValue; a JObject can be indexed by key (model.nested['p1']); and a missing key on a System.Text.Json object is null, as with property access, rather than an error.
Fixed: text that carries on from the line before onto a line with a taller image or inline block on the baseline was drawn too high - above the baseline of the image, and the text after it. It is now on the same baseline.
Fixed: fonts whose licence flags combine restricted with preview and print or editable embedding (e.g. 0x0006, as many system fonts like Gill Sans) were not embedded, so a viewer drew another font. The least restrictive flag is used, as the OpenType specification says. With Scryber.Core.OpenType 9.7.5 a font from a collection (.ttc) is embedded as a valid font of its own.
Fixed: the num element read its value attribute as zero - only data-value was read. value is now the same as data-value (as the html data, meter and progress elements), e.g. <num value="{{.price}}" data-format="C2" />.

9.9.1
Fixed: an image or inline block with vertical-align: baseline after one with another alignment (e.g. top) on the same line moved the text of the line down to the bottom of the line. Baseline items no longer change the alignment of the line.
Changed: date() reads text in the current culture first, then the invariant culture, so English month and day names and AM/PM are read on any machine or browser (e.g. date('January 15, 2024', 'MMMM dd, yyyy') under de-DE). Text that reads in the current culture is read the same as before.

9.9.0
Breaking change: a css transform no longer changes the layout. A transformed element keeps its place and space in the flow (it was taken out as position: absolute, and its space was resized to the transformed bounds), and is drawn transformed around the centre of its own border box. Before, the centre was worked out from the wrong place, so a rotated element (e.g. rotate(-90deg)) was drawn away from where it should be. A relative element is moved by its left and top, then transformed around its moved centre. An absolute or fixed element stays absolute or fixed.
New: the transform-origin css property, with keywords (left, center, right, top, bottom), lengths and percentages. Percentages are of the element's own border box.
Breaking change: translate() percentages are of the element's own border box (they were of the containing block), so translate(-50%, -50%) centres an element on its position.
Breaking change: a translate after another operation is along the transformed axes, as css (e.g. rotate(90deg) translate(50pt, 0) moves 50pt down the page). It was always along the page axes. This is the same for an svg transform attribute.
Fixed: flattening a transform with more than one operation changed the shared style rather than the copy, so elements with the same class could use the values of another element.

9.8.2
The package description and NuGet readme now introduce Paperwork.Core as the successor to Scryber.Core, with Scryber.Core as its engine - still maintained and supported. No code changes from 9.8.1.

9.8.1
The 9.8.1 release: everything in the 9.8.0 betas below, including document permissions and passwords, encryption in the browser (Blazor WASM), and the CSS layout additions.

9.8.0-beta.12
Fixed: a secured (encrypted) document failed in the browser (Blazor WASM), as MD5 is not available there - the PDF security handler now uses its own managed MD5 on every platform.

9.8.0-beta.11
Fixed: allowing modifications (document assembly) in a secured document also allowed high quality printing, and cleared a reserved permission bit.
Fixed: allowing forms in a secured document also allowed annotations.
Fixed: a document password longer than 32 characters failed the document - only the first 32 characters are used, as in the PDF specification. A password with characters outside Latin-1 is a clear error.

9.8.0-beta.10
Fixed: flex items without a width that hold a block, a flex column or a flex row are the width of their content (they were the full width of the row, so justify-content had no space to share and items overlapped, wrapped or ran off the page). An empty flex item has no width.
Fixed: justify-content takes the flex container's own margins from its width, and the gaps are part of the space used, so the last item is on the right edge.
Fixed: position: absolute with a left and a right but no width is stretched between them. A max-width still limits it.
Fixed: counter-increment on a display: grid or display: table element is counted.
New: a trace log warning when a counter-increment finds no counter-reset on the element or a containing element.
Changed: the background shorthand sets all the background values (any not given are back to their defaults), reads none, position and size (center / cover), accepts and ignores scroll, fixed and the box keywords, draws a color under an image, and is ignored as a whole if any part cannot be read.
New: box-decoration-break (and -webkit-box-decoration-break) - clone (the default, a full border on each part of a split block) or slice (the border is cut at the break).

9.8.0-beta.9
Fixed: a gradient that cannot be drawn (e.g. a stop with 2 positions) is not drawn and the background-color is kept, with a warning in the trace log, rather than failing the document with No boundaries were provided.
Fixed: transparent in a gradient is drawn as black, with a warning in the trace log, rather than failing the document with Cannot convert colorspace None to RGB.
Fixed: the line height in the font shorthand (e.g. font: 10.5pt/1.65 sans-serif) is read as a css number, not in the language of the machine or browser.
Fixed: numbers held as text (e.g. json or field values) are read the same as numbers in the expression, in calculations, functions and comparisons, whatever the language of the machine or browser. Numbers and dates written out as text still use that language.
Fixed: decimal values in transform, svg transform and orient, and picture sizes are read as css numbers.

9.8.0-beta.8
Fixed: linear-gradient color stops can be a length (e.g. var(--accent) 112pt), so two colors at the same position are a hard stop; rgb() stops with a position keep their color.
Fixed: box-shadow with a var() in the value (e.g. 9pt 9pt 0 var(--accent)) is drawn.
Fixed: an image with only a height in a flex header or continuation-header is shown on the first page the header is used.
Fixed: letter-spacing and word-spacing in em are of the element's own font size, not the inherited one.
New: display inline-flex, inline-grid and inline-table - an inline block with flex, grid or table content.
Changed: a word that is longer than the line is kept whole and overflows (as a browser). Use overflow-wrap: break-word to break it.

9.8.0-beta.7
Fixed: flex items without a width, flex-basis or flex-grow are the width of their content (measured by a layout that is discarded - counters, ::before/::after, names, outlines and page breaks are not affected). They had no width, so next to a growing item they disappeared.
Changed: a flex row of only content width items is packed at the start (as css) rather than split into equal columns.

9.8.0-beta.6
New css: margin-block, padding-block (and -start, -end), inset, inset-block and inset-inline (and -start, -end). cursor, pointer-events, will-change, scroll-behavior, user-select, transition and animation are accepted and ignored.
Changed: overflow: hidden on text that does not wrap cuts the text back to the last whole word that fits (overflow: clip is still a clipping rectangle).
Fixed: the items in a flex row stretch to the height of the row (align-items: stretch, the default), unless they have a height or align-self/align-items says otherwise.
Fixed: inline flex items (span) are blockified - width, margins, filling the column, stacking in a column and align-items centring now work.
Fixed: a percentage border-radius is of the width of the box (not the container) and radii are limited so they are never larger than a side - 50% on a square is a circle, not a star.
Fixed: counter-increment and counter-reset on table rows (tr) are updated once per row.

9.8.0-beta.5
New css: word-break (break-all fills each line, breaking a word at any character with no hyphen), overflow-wrap and word-wrap (accepted, long words are always broken), and text-overflow (ellipsis, clip or a string, for non-wrapping text in a block with overflow hidden or clip).
Fixed: a negative text-indent is a hanging indent. The first line only starts out, and the following lines (and any text after a line break) start at the edge of the content.

9.8.0-beta.4
Fixed: visibility: collapse on a table row (or thead, tbody, tfoot) removes the rows and their space, as display: none does. On other elements it is the same as hidden.
Fixed: border-collapse and border-spacing are inherited as in css, so they can be set on a container or the body. Added the table cellspacing attribute (a number is pixels), overridden by any css border-spacing.
Fixed: box-shadow and outline are drawn for images (inline and block), they were only drawn for blocks and tables.

9.8.0-beta.3
New css: text-decoration-color, text-decoration-style (solid, double, dotted, dashed, wavy) and text-decoration-thickness, also in the text-decoration shorthand; outline, outline-color, outline-style, outline-width and outline-offset; box-shadow (offset, blur, spread, colour, multiple, rounded corners); text-shadow.
Fixed: an inline image (or other drawn component) with a margin was drawn at its size plus the margins, over the margin area. It is now drawn at its own size inside the margin.
New: sortBy(values) and sortBy(values, 'desc') sort plain values such as the result of keys().
Fixed: sortBy with items that have the same sort value threw an error. They are now kept in their original order.

9.8.0-beta.2
New: keys() function - the keys of a dictionary or the property names of an object, as an array that can be counted, sorted and enumerated.
New css: text-indent; box-sizing (content-box is the opt-in, the default already includes the padding in the width); border-collapse and border-spacing for tables; object-fit and object-position for raster images; visibility (hidden content keeps its space but is not drawn).
Fixed: collection functions (sortBy, sumOf, averageOf, minOf, maxOf, countOf, eachOf, selectWhere, firstWhere) accept a quoted property name ('price', 'owner.city') as well as .price.
Fixed: a property named e, pi, true, false or null after '.' or '../' (e.g. model.e) is read as the property, not the constant.
Fixed: join() accepts join(collection, separator) as well as join(separator, items...).

9.8.0-beta
New: text-transform css property (none, uppercase, lowercase, capitalize) - inherited, and usable with expressions.
New: @first and @last loop variables alongside @index, usable in output, {{#if}}, if() and css expressions. @last is correct for arrays, lists, dictionaries and Linq iterators.
New: @key loop variable - the key or property name when iterating a dictionary or json object, or the index for a collection. It is restored after each (nested) loop.
Changed: {{#each}} over a Dictionary, a Newtonsoft JObject or a System.Text.Json object now iterates the entries (as in Handlebars) rather than binding the object once. The template element and ForEach component still bind an object once.
Fixed: ../ inside {{#each}} now refers to the outer item (or {{#with}} object) rather than the collection being enumerated. It is a single level only.
Fixed: {{#each}} over a non-resettable enumerable (e.g. a Linq Select) threw 'Specified method is not supported' in strict mode.
Fixed: var() and calc() inside linear-gradient() and radial-gradient() dropped the gradient, and the background shorthand now accepts gradients.
Fixed: Fonts:Register entries now apply their Weight and Style, rather than the weight and style of the font file.
Fixed: the HTML5 parser now accepts the paperwork processing instruction as well as scryber. Added Document.ParseDocument and ParseHtmlDocument overloads (and async) that take ParserSettings.
Fixed: configured image factory handlers (ImageFactoryCustom) can now decode streams supplied by a requestor on a custom path.
Fixed: parsed collections accept an Add method of a base type (e.g. [PDFArray(typeof(Panel))] on a ComponentList), and components derived from Panel keep their child content.
Obsolete: the HtmlFragment component.

9.7.5
Consistent error handling in strict and lax mode - invalid syntax is invalid completely, missing data is not a syntax error.
Invalid expression syntax now always throws, in strict and lax: an expression that is incomplete when evaluated (e.g. model.items[0), a function with the wrong number of parameters, and an invalid expression inside a repeating or conditional template ({{#each}}, {{#if}}). Lax previously logged these and carried on.
A root variable that is not set (or is null) logs a single error in both modes (strict previously threw). A null part way along, or at the end of, a path (e.g. model.missing.value where missing or value is null) is silent and just results in null.
CSS var() and calc() follow the same rules: var(model.x, default) uses the default when there is no value, and invalid css expressions are validated and raised when the css is parsed.
Document.CreateParserSettings() and CreateParserSettingsAsync() now default to Lax, matching Document.ParseDocument().
Added int() as a short name for integer(). Corrected the function documentation to the registered names monthOf, deg, rad, isMatch, matches and swap.

9.7.4.4
Fixed a colspan cell's nested content (paragraphs, text) being squeezed into its starting column's width instead of the full spanned width - the cell's outer box was already sized correctly, but content layout took a stale single-column width at face value.
Removed Overflow.Split = Never from <figure>, which forced any figure content (not just an image+caption pair) to be treated as an unsplittable block and crashed when a wrapped table was too tall to fit on one page.

9.7.4.3
Fixed a colspan cell silently losing the width of any <col>/<colgroup> column that is never singly occupied by a cell in any row (e.g. a 3-column percentage colgroup where every row crosses the middle column with a colspan) - that column's width is now resolved through the normal style pipeline, so percent/em/rem/viewport units, calc() and var() all work correctly.

9.7.4.2
Fixed image aspect-ratio sizing to also honour max-width/max-height/min-width/min-height clamping and re-derive the other dimension from aspect-ratio when both width and height were already resolved (e.g. an img sized only via its HTML width/height attributes inside a percentage-width figure) - previously that combination bypassed clamping and aspect-ratio entirely.
Rebuilt <hr> as a genuine box-model block element (border-*, background-color, height, width, margin) instead of a stroked diagonal-line path - standard CSS resets like `border: none; height: 4pt; background-color: ...;` now render a proper coloured bar instead of a diagonal line, while a bare <hr> keeps its familiar default 1pt solid black border-bottom.

9.7.4.1
Minor fix to HTML5 layout engine bindings: display:table/grid now correctly wrap loose content generated by {{#each}}/{{#with}}/{{#if}} instead of dropping it or leaving a spurious empty cell, and a loose display:inline-block child is treated leniently as block rather than rendering blank. Also adds support for the CSS Display Module 3 two-value display syntax (e.g. "block flex", "inline flow-root") alongside the existing single-keyword values.

9.7.4
Fixed a data race in PDFFontWidths (font glyph registration) that could corrupt concurrently-rendered documents' text under multi-threaded rendering, sometimes silently writing wrong glyphs with no exception raised. Contributed by twofatmonkeys (PR #186).
Updated the Scryber.Core.OpenType dependency to 9.7.4, fixing a companion data race in TTFStringMeasurer's glyph metric cache under the same multi-threaded rendering conditions. Neither fix alone makes concurrent rendering safe - both are required.

9.7.3
Fixed a display:table container (e.g. a designer-authored figure wrapping an image) silently dropping any loose non table-row/table-cell child from layout, including never registering it as a PDF image resource.

9.7.2
Fixed :nth-child/:nth-of-type not correctly counting siblings across an IInvisibleContainer wrapper (e.g. {{#each}}-generated content), which previously made every generated item compute itself as an isolated "1 of 1".
Fixed flex row items requiring a Panel-derived component - non-container children (e.g. bare text nodes) are now wrapped in a new InvisibleFlexContainer so they get a proper block-layout box.
Fixed an XML/HTML parser bug where an element immediately (no whitespace) after {{/each}} could be silently dropped from the component tree when it shared its outer container's tag name.

9.7.0
BREAKING CHANGE: <img width>/<img height> already accepted integer pixels only (from 9.6.0.7-beta); now correctly documented as a breaking change for this major version bump.
Added CSS aspect-ratio support for images and block elements.
Added colgroup/col table column support with width, background-color, and span.
Added CSS grid: grid-template-areas, grid-area, named grid lines, auto-fill/auto-fit in repeat(), grid-auto-columns/rows, justify-content and align-content.
Added flex align-items for column-direction flex containers.
Added CSS var()/calc() support in flex and grid CSS properties.
Fixed SVG image min/max-width/height sizing across all four sizing strategies, with correct aspect-ratio preservation.
Fixed SVG image 300x150 clipping bug for unsized SVG images (canvas now sized from page).
Fixed page-break-after followed by page-break-before producing a redundant blank page.
Fixed CSS var()/calc() silent failures (no longer drops entire style block on unbound expressions).
Various flex, grid, list, font, and layout bug fixes.

Earlier versions: https://paperwork.help/paperwork.core/changelog/scryber_core.html
